title: "RQA Tutorial Worksheet"
format: html
---

In this tutorial, we are going to work through using the crqa package to run a Recurrence Quantification Analysis (RQA) on categorical data. Any kind of categorical data will work, but we're going to use texts as an example. 

# Step 1. Setup your workspace
Here, we're going to load in the appropriate packages

tidyverse is a swiss-army knife for data wrangling. I don't actually think we need it, but it's good to have

crqa is the package that will do our analysis.

gt is for making tables quickly.

```{r, warning=FALSE}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse) 
library(crqa)
library(gt)

```

# Step 2. Load our data
The example dataset is in a csv called "texts.csv".
Your data doesn't have to be text, its just a convenient example.
Your data does need to be organized in columns though. 

```{r}
texts <- read.csv("texts.csv")
```

# Step 3. Get your parameters right
(this is an information only step)
In our case, because we're using categorical data, we can use standard values for our parameters. 

Inside the crqa function, we're going to set these values:

delay = 1,
embed = 1,
rescale = 0,
radius = 0.001,
normalize = 0,
mindiagline = 2,
minvertline = 2,
tw = 0,
whiteline = FALSE,
recpt = FALSE,
side = "both",
method = "rqa",
metric = "euclidean",
datatype = "categorical"

I will mention the important ones in the lecture. For additional information, type ?crqa in the console.

# Step 4. Let's run an RQA

One of the "texts" is the first ~150 words of Moby Dick. This will be our first example. 

Some important things:
1) we're writing the function to an object using the <- operator
2) we need to specify the data twice as ts1 and ts2 (short for timeseries 1 & 2)
3) because the data is a part of a larger dataset, we need to call it using the $ operator

```{r}
moby_for_plot <- crqa(ts1 = texts$moby,
                 ts2 = texts$moby,
                 delay = 1,
                 embed = 1,
                 rescale = 0,
                 radius = 0.001,
                 normalize = 0,
                 mindiagline = 2,
                 minvertline = 2,
                 tw = 0,
                 whiteline = FALSE,
                 recpt = FALSE,
                 side = "both",
                 method = "rqa",
                 metric = "euclidean",
                 datatype = "categorical")
```

# Step 5: Let's see the plot
You might have noticed that the object is called "moby_for_plot".

This is because we need to change one of the parameters before we get our output metrics. More on that later.

We can use the native plotting function in crqa (plot_rp).

Here, we need to use the $ operator again to call the RP (recurrence plot) that is saved in the object that was created in the previous step (moby_for_plot).

We don't have to write the plot to an object because we want to see the output immediately. You can do that, and it is useful for some things, we just are not doing it now. 

```{r}
plot_rp(moby_for_plot$RP,
                  title = "Recurrence Plot of the first ~150 words of Moby Dick",
                  xlabel = "Call me Ishmael...",
                  ylabel = "Call me Ishmael...",
                  pcolour = "black",
                  geom = c("void"),
                  flip_y = FALSE) +
                    geom_point(size = 1)
```

# Step 6. Metrics

Ok, the plot's nice. But we're scientists! We want numbers!

We need to run the crqa function again, this time with tw=1. This will remove the diagonal (the line of identity) from our calculations. 

Notice that we're saving this as a new object (moby_for_metric)

```{r}
moby_for_metric <- crqa(ts1 = texts$moby,
                 ts2 = texts$moby,
                 delay = 1,
                 embed = 1,
                 rescale = 0,
                 radius = 0.001,
                 normalize = 0,
                 mindiagline = 2,
                 minvertline = 2,
                 tw = 1,
                 whiteline = FALSE,
                 recpt = FALSE,
                 side = "both",
                 method = "rqa",
                 metric = "euclidean",
                 datatype = "categorical")
```


And now we need to make a home for our metrics (moby_output) and pull them out of the moby_for_metric object.

- Recurrence Rate (RR) is the proportion of recurrent points
- Determinism (DET) is the propotion of points on diagonal lines
- Number of lines (NRLINE) is... the number of (diagonal) lines
- Maximum Line (MaxL) is the longest line
- Average line length (L) is the average diagonal line length
- Entropy (ENTR) is the observed probability of lines of all possible lengths... you know what, don't worry about this one and please do not ask me about it. It's all gonna be fine.
- Laminarity (LAM) is DET for vertical lines
- Trapping Time (TT) is L for vertical lines

gt is gonna organize these into a neat little table for us.

```{r}
moby_output <- data.frame()

moby_output <- rbind(moby_output,
                       cbind("RR" = moby_for_metric$RR,
                             "DET" = moby_for_metric$DET,
                             "NRLINE" = moby_for_metric$NRLINE,
                             "MaxL" = moby_for_metric$maxL,
                             "L" = moby_for_metric$L,
                             "ENTR" = moby_for_metric$ENTR,
                             "LAM" = moby_for_metric$LAM,
                             "TT" = moby_for_metric$TT))

gt(moby_output)
```

# Step 7. Now it's your turn
At this point in the talk, we've walked through an example.
We're about to do a couple more. This time though, you get to do some typing instead of just hitting the little green arrow.

Our next example is a poem by Dylan Thomas, labelled "death" in our texts dataset. 

your job is to call the right dataset here. You need to enter in the correct values for ts1 and ts2 (where the ? are).

```{r}
death_for_plot <- crqa(ts1 = texts$?,
                 ts2 = texts$?,
                 delay = 1,
                 embed = 1,
                 rescale = 0,
                 radius = 0.001,
                 normalize = 0,
                 mindiagline = 2,
                 minvertline = 2,
                 tw = 0,
                 whiteline = FALSE,
                 recpt = FALSE,
                 side = "both",
                 method = "rqa",
                 metric = "euclidean",
                 datatype = "categorical")
```

and of course, we'll want to see that plot.

Now you need to call the correct part of the death_for_plot object

```{r}

plot_rp(death_for_plot$?,
                  title = "Recurrence Plot of And Death Shall Have No Dominion",
                  xlabel = "And Death Shall Have No Dominion...",
                  ylabel = "And Death Shall Have No Dominion...",
                  pcolour = "black",
                  geom = c("void"),
                  flip_y = FALSE) +
                    geom_point(size = 1)

```

Good work! (I assume).

Now we'll make it a little harder (as in, you have to copy-paste more).

In the next code block, you need to fill in the whole crqa function for the text "wheels" (it's The Wheels on the Bus). Again, this is mostly a copy paste, but you have to make sure you're calling the right data.

```{r}
wheels_for_plot <- crqa()
  
  
```


Now do the same for the plot:

For the title use: "Recurrence Plot of The Wheels on the Bus"
For the xlabel and ylabel use: "The wheels on the bus go..."

```{r}
plot_rp()
```

You're doing great! (probably)

Now we need to get metrics from both these RPs.

First, we need to run the crqa function for both again with the tw value changed. It is NOT changed in the codeblock below. You must change the value of tw before running this block.


```{r}

death_for_metric <- crqa(ts1 = texts$death,
                 ts2 = texts$death,
                 delay = 1,
                 embed = 1,
                 rescale = 0,
                 radius = 0.001,
                 normalize = 0,
                 mindiagline = 2,
                 minvertline = 2,
                 tw = 0,
                 whiteline = FALSE,
                 recpt = FALSE,
                 side = "both",
                 method = "rqa",
                 metric = "euclidean",
                 datatype = "categorical")

wheels_for_metric <- crqa(ts1 = texts$wheels,
                 ts2 = texts$wheels,
                 delay = 1,
                 embed = 1,
                 rescale = 0,
                 radius = 0.001,
                 normalize = 0,
                 mindiagline = 2,
                 minvertline = 2,
                 tw = 0,
                 whiteline = FALSE,
                 recpt = FALSE,
                 side = "both",
                 method = "rqa",
                 metric = "euclidean",
                 datatype = "categorical")

```

Ok, now we need to extract the metrics.

Fill in the ? with the correct type of object. 

```{r}
death_output <- ?

death_output <- rbind(death_output,
                       cbind("RR" = death_for_metric$RR,
                             "DET" = death_for_metric$DET,
                             "NRLINE" = death_for_metric$NRLINE,
                             "MaxL" = death_for_metric$maxL,
                             "L" = death_for_metric$L,
                             "ENTR" = death_for_metric$ENTR,
                             "LAM" = death_for_metric$LAM,
                             "TT" = death_for_metric$TT))

wheels_output <- ?

wheels_output <- rbind(wheels_output,
                       cbind("RR" = wheels_for_metric$RR,
                             "DET" = wheels_for_metric$DET,
                             "NRLINE" = wheels_for_metric$NRLINE,
                             "MaxL" = wheels_for_metric$maxL,
                             "L" = wheels_for_metric$L,
                             "ENTR" = wheels_for_metric$ENTR,
                             "LAM" = wheels_for_metric$LAM,
                             "TT" = wheels_for_metric$TT))
```

Help, I'm alive (that's a Metric reference)

Ok, now we want to bring all the metrics together. You do not need to make any changes to the following block. If you did everything right so far, it should run ok.

```{r}

rqa_metrics <- rbind("wheels" = wheels_output, "moby" = moby_output, "death" = death_output)

gt(rqa_metrics, rownames_to_stub = TRUE)

```


Congratulations - this is where we watch the boulder roll down the hill, and like Sisyphus, we trudge down and commence to rolling it up once more. 

To aid you in your perpetual boulder rolling, here's a template:

```{r}
data <- read.csv(path/to/your/data)

rqa_for_plot <- crqa(crqa(ts1 = data,
                 ts2 = data,
                 delay = 1,
                 embed = 1,
                 rescale = 0,
                 radius = 0.001,
                 normalize = 0,
                 mindiagline = 2,
                 minvertline = 2,
                 tw = 0,
                 whiteline = FALSE,
                 recpt = FALSE,
                 side = "both",
                 method = "rqa",
                 metric = "euclidean",
                 datatype = "categorical"))

plot_rp(rqa_for_plot$RP,
                  title = "Recurrence Plot of Your Date",
                  xlabel = "Your Data...",
                  ylabel = "Your Data...",
                  pcolour = "black",
                  geom = c("void"),
                  flip_y = FALSE) +
                    geom_point(size = 1)

rqa_for_metric <- crqa(crqa(ts1 = data,
                 ts2 = data,
                 delay = 1,
                 embed = 1,
                 rescale = 0,
                 radius = 0.001,
                 normalize = 0,
                 mindiagline = 2,
                 minvertline = 2,
                 tw = 1,
                 whiteline = FALSE,
                 recpt = FALSE,
                 side = "both",
                 method = "rqa",
                 metric = "euclidean",
                 datatype = "categorical"))

data_output <- data.frame()

data_output <- rbind(data_output,
                       cbind("RR" = rqa_for_metric$RR,
                             "DET" = rqa_for_metric$DET,
                             "NRLINE" = rqa_for_metric$NRLINE,
                             "MaxL" = rqa_for_metric$maxL,
                             "L" = rqa_for_metric$L,
                             "ENTR" = rqa_for_metric$ENTR,
                             "LAM" = rqa_for_metric$LAM,
                             "TT" = rqa_for_metric$TT))

```

There's a whole lot more you can do with the crqa package. For more info, see the paper here: DOI: 10.32614/RJ-2021-062 

Thanks for playing!
